title: k-NN, k-means and the tree split

wrong.knn_nearest_only.py: knn_predict ignores k and votes with only the single nearest neighbour
wrong.knn_tie_to_largest.py: knn_predict breaks a tied vote toward the largest label instead of the smallest
wrong.knn_unstable_sort.py: knn_predict uses an unstable sort, so equal distances are not resolved by training order
wrong.kmeans_empty_to_zero.py: kmeans_update sends an empty cluster's centre to the origin instead of keeping it
wrong.kmeans_modifies_centers.py: kmeans_update writes into the caller's centres array
wrong.gini_uses_entropy.py: gini returns the entropy -sum(p log2 p) instead of 1 - sum(p^2)
wrong.split_unweighted_children.py: best_split averages the two child impurities without weighting by child size
wrong.split_picks_last_tie.py: best_split keeps the last of several equally good thresholds instead of the first

hints: Distances: (Xte[:, None, :] - Xtr[None, :, :]) ** 2 summed over the last axis gives an (m, n) matrix of squared distances. Squared distance orders neighbours the same as distance, so skip the sqrt. np.argsort with kind="stable" keeps training order among equal distances, and np.unique returns sorted labels, which makes the smallest-label tie rule free.

K-means: assignment is an argmin over the (n, k) distance matrix; the update is a per-cluster mean. Guard the empty cluster (members.size == 0) so you do not take the mean of nothing. Copy the centres before writing.

Tree split: sort the distinct values, take midpoints, and score each with the size-weighted child impurity (n_left * G_left + n_right * G_right) / n. Accept a candidate only if it beats the best so far by more than a tiny epsilon, so the first (smallest) of tied thresholds wins and a no-gain split returns (None, 0.0).
